description: ICS Village at DEF CON 27 covers critical infrastructure security, industrial control systems vulnerabilities, and attacks on operational technology. The 11 talks explore SCADA systems, supply chain attacks, IT/OT convergence, smart building security, and defensive strategies for industrial networks.

talks.title: Changium IPiosa  magical change IP packets in the wild
talks.teaser: IP packet manipulation techniques for network-based attacks on industrial systems.
talks.summary:
### Uncovering Undocumented Network Protocols in Industrial Hardware
At 00:00, industrial security researchers Sharon Brizinov and Tom present research on reversing proprietary network protocols in industrial automation hardware at the ICS Village.

### Discovery Protocols and Magic Configuration Packets
At 05:07, the speakers examine how industrial devices—such as PLCs, serial device servers, and protocol gateways—are deployed in the field. To facilitate easy installation, manufacturers implement lightweight UDP broadcast daemons that listen for magic packet sequences to configure device network settings.

### Arbitrary Command Execution via Management Daemons
At 10:21, the presentation demonstrates severe vulnerabilities within these configuration routines. By reverse-engineering proprietary firmware binaries, the researchers discovered that unauthenticated broadcast packets could be crafted to inject operating system commands directly into embedded device shells.

### Network Disruption via Remote IP Alteration
At 15:30, the authors illustrate attack scenarios against operational facilities. An unauthenticated attacker transmitting crafted broadcast frames across local network segments can silently alter the IP addresses and subnet masks of critical PLCs, instantly severing communication between controllers and SCADA monitoring stations.

### Insecure Proprietary Cryptography and Vendor Remediation
Concluding between 20:41 and 25:33, the researchers expose the weak security controls implemented by vendors. They reveal protocols that claimed to be encrypted but relied entirely on static XOR keys, outlining defensive recommendations and firmware remediation guidelines for industrial equipment manufacturers.

talks.title: Purple Teaming ICS Networks
talks.teaser: Collaborative red and blue team exercises for industrial network security validation.
talks.summary:
In this talk from the DEF CON 27 ICS Village, Austin Scott explores the principles, methodology, and operational value of executing purple team engagements within Industrial Control System (ICS) and SCADA environments. He introduces the spectrum of testing approaches at 03:00, contrasting black box and gray box assessments with collaborative white box purple teaming, where offensive operators and defensive defenders work together in real time. At 06:00, he explains the crucial role of the blue team in supplying network topologies, baseline packet captures, and system telemetry to maximize testing efficiency.

Austin addresses the unique constraints of OT environments at 09:00, emphasizing that operational safety, plant availability, and the physical stability of programmable logic controllers (PLCs) must take precedence over aggressive penetration testing techniques. At 12:00, he analyzes proprietary industrial protocols and segmented Purdue Model topologies, followed by a case study at 15:00 examining a purple team assessment conducted on a major electrical power utility. He details the attack path from initial enterprise breach to plant control networks at 18:00.

The presentation emphasizes real-time validation at 21:00, where red team attack emulations are synchronized directly with blue team detection engineering to identify visibility blind spots in SIEM rules and network sensors. At 24:00, Austin discusses auditing against corporate ICS security frameworks, and at 27:00, he demonstrates automated log ingestion pipelines using Python parsers and Elasticsearch to rapidly turn red team findings into resilient defensive detections. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: ICS IOT Threat Landscape
talks.teaser: Current threat landscape and emerging vulnerabilities in ICS and IoT systems.
talks.summary:
### Convergence and Threat Modeling Across ICS and IoT
At 00:00, Bryson Bort, founder of SCYTHE and GRIMM, delivers an operational overview of the expanding threat landscape across industrial control systems (ICS) and enterprise Internet of Things (IoT) at the ICS Village.

### Societal Dependencies on Operational Technology
At 04:34, Bort highlights the critical dependencies underpinning modern civilization. He emphasizes that disruptions to electrical generation, water treatment, and transportation networks carry physical consequences that far exceed the impact of traditional enterprise data breaches.

### Adversary Deception and False-Flag Operations
At 09:23, the presentation explores the complexity of threat attribution in OT incidents. Bort explains how sophisticated adversaries deliberately employ false language artifacts, open-source penetration tools, and multi-layered proxy networks to mislead threat intelligence investigators.

### Inherent Trust in Industrial Field Protocols
At 14:00, Bort addresses a core structural vulnerability of operational technology: lack of native authentication. Industrial field devices (such as PLCs and RTUs) execute commands implicitly without verifying sender identity, meaning attackers do not require zero-day exploits if they can access engineering network segments.

### Supply Chain Risk and IoT Gateway Exposure
Concluding between 18:45 and 24:09, the speaker discusses the risks of unmanaged enterprise IoT deployments. He cautions that insecure smart building sensors and remote maintenance gateways frequently act as unprotected bridges connecting enterprise IT environments directly to sensitive operational networks.

talks.title: HVACking: The difference Between Security and Reality
talks.teaser: Security vulnerabilities in HVAC systems and the gap between theory and practice.
talks.summary:
In this talk at the DEF CON 27 ICS Village, Douglas McKee from McAfee ATR shares his research uncovering critical vulnerabilities in commercial building automation and HVAC management systems. He introduces the investigation into Delta Controls ORCAview BACnet controllers at 04:00, walking through how he identified a remote heap-based memory corruption vulnerability in the device's network stack. He details the challenge of exploiting constrained microcontroller memory and executing arbitrary shellcode on embedded architectures.

Douglas explains how building automation systems rely on the BACnet protocol at 08:00, detailing how broadcast UDP restrictions were circumvented to make the attack routeable and exploitable across the public internet. At 12:00, he presents a firmware function hooking technique that enables an attacker to manipulate low-level input/output (I/O) control registers directly in microcontroller memory, establishing persistent, stealthy control over heating, ventilation, and cooling hardware.

At 16:00, Douglas outlines the severe real-world ramifications of compromised HVAC systems in sensitive environments such as hospitals, laboratories, and mission-critical data centers. He concludes with a live demonstration at 20:00, illustrating an attacker secretly altering physical temperature setpoints while tampering with the operator GUI to display normal operating conditions. At 24:00, he provides defensive recommendations for isolating building automation networks and preventing unauthorized protocol access. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: IT OT Convergence Are We There Yet
talks.teaser: Integration challenges and security implications of IT and OT network convergence.
talks.summary:
### Realities and Cultural Friction in IT/OT Convergence
At 00:00, Jack Oden from Parsons Government Systems presents an operational assessment of the technical and cultural friction between Information Technology (IT) and Operational Technology (OT) teams at the ICS Village.

### The Evolution of Industrial Automation
At 05:00, Oden traces the technological evolution of industrial plants. He explains how industrial processes transitioned from isolated pneumatic systems and dedicated serial wiring into networked supervisory control architectures connected via Ethernet and TCP/IP.

### The Cultural Divide: Enterprise IT vs. Plant Engineering
At 10:06, the presentation examines the differing priorities governing IT and OT personnel. While IT departments prioritize data confidentiality, regular software patching, and system reboots, plant engineers prioritize continuous availability, process safety, and deterministic real-time control.

### Challenges of Legacy Systems in Production
At 14:48, Oden explains why decades-old operating systems remain active in industrial facilities. Taking production lines offline to patch systems introduces substantial financial and operational risks, leading plant operators to resist updates unless absolutely necessary.

### Frameworks for Successful Convergence
Concluding between 19:32 and 24:41, Oden outlines a maturity model for IT/OT convergence. He provides guidance for fostering empathy between engineers and security teams, encouraging cross-training and shared governance to protect critical infrastructure without compromising operational reliability.
